utterances.text: All right. Thank you. There was already a list of wounded there. Who did you get the list from?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: We didn't get them from anybody. It was stuck to the door, the entrance door, the list was there, taped to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you were sent to the morgue, the mortuary?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Not straight away. I stayed there for half an hour, looking at all the lists. There wasn't just one list. I was looking for my wife's name on one of the lists, but I didn't find it. And then a doctor came by, and I asked him and he directed me to the mortuary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What mortuary was that? Was it within the Kosevo Hospital compound?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: It was to the left, looking at it from "cum," [phoen] near that semi-circular building, you know that semi-circular building, well the mortuary is next to that. You know where that is, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to that. I'm just waiting for the interpretation to finish. So is that the mortuary at one of the exits, which is where it always was, the exit towards the faculty of architecture, that way?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what did you see when you entered the mortuary? How many bodies were there? What position were they in?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: When I reached the mortuary, I can't tell you the exact number but there were about nine, about nine bodies, and they were all lying on their backs. When I came to my wife, there was a woman lying next to my wife and her arm was thrown across my wife's body. I just cried. As soon as they heard my voice in one of the other rooms, three men came out straight away and asked me what had happened, whether I'd recognised my wife, and I said, Yes, that's her, it's this one here. They took a note of that. They showed me the wound where she had been hit, and I asked to be given a document straight away, some kind of document stating that in the massacre my wife had been killed. But they didn't want to give me that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who were the other eight bodies? Were they male or female?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Mostly women.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If it's not too difficult for you to talk about it, could you tell us where your wife was wounded? Where was the wound?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: It was in her left shoulder. A shrapnel from the shell hit her in her left shoulder blade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And your wife was wearing clothes, of course?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the other 40 dead, where were they?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: They were in another room from where those three men came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that same mortuary?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, in the same mortuary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With everybody's permission, I would like to go back to that tomorrow and ask permission for us to add another piece of evidence to throw some more light on the topic that Mr. Crncalo has just talked to us about. And I'm very thankful to him for that, despite -- I know it's very difficult for him and very emotional for him to speak about it, but thank you for -- I'd like to thank him for testifying about it. Do we still have a little time, Your Excellency, because I'd like to go back to one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I just ask for clarification, is the additional item of evidence -- I would like the accused to clarify whether that's on the list disclosed by the Defence at the commencement of the cross-examination or is that an additional item of evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was about to ask the same question. So we have still five or seven minutes for that. So if you have anything to further examine the witness, you may do so, and if you could clarify what you meant by adding evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll be happy to do that. Yes, that's quite right. It's an exhibit that was not announced, and this came about because Mr. Crncalo described to us a situation in which he was an eye-witness, and that was more exhaustive than was the description given in his statement. So he described to us what he had seen, where he went, where he came from, where he went, what he saw at the site itself, and this requires the Defence to put forward another piece of evidence. Had we known that Mr. Crncalo would be speaking about the site itself in the way he did, we would have done that and produced that evidence. But the exhibit will be presented in many other cases. We're just going to show one or two pieces of that evidence tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should let the Prosecution know what they are about during the course of today, and then we'll hear from the Prosecution and decide whether to allow the accused to adduce this evidence. Is there any questions -- are there any questions to put to the witness today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps I could go back to the beginning if we have time, the beginning of his statement. Well, I don't want to belabour this topic which is a very painful one for Mr. Crncalo, but if we have time, I can go back to the beginning of the statement or should we leave it for tomorrow? Whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have five minutes. We can use as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, you said that at the high court in Sarajevo on the 23rd of August, 2005 [as interpreted], you gave a statement. That was five days before your wife was killed; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: You mean before her death?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: On the 23rd of August, 1995, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1995, that's five days before your wife was killed.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Or was that after the death of your wife?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I think they asked me during that hearing about my wife's death. I think that's what they asked me. They asked me about my wife being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean in that statement?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this statement is not sufficient?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: May I add something? If no mention is made of my wife's death in that statement, then that means it was before, that it was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. In any case, we need that statement in order to be able to establish the circumstances. So I kindly request the opposite side to provide that for us because this amalgamated statement does not cover that fact. So we do need that other statement. Now, to go back to the beginning of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just clarify, the statement of the witness, which was given on the 23rd of August, 1995, has, to the best of my knowledge, already been disclosed to the Defence in English and in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's my understanding. I will re-check it, but I'm pretty much 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for convenience, could you make another photocopy and disclose it to the accused today?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, as Your Honour wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see the time. We'll adjourn and rise for today, and we'll resume tomorrow at 9.00. But during the adjournment, Mr. Crncalo, you should not discuss your evidence with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. I know about that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of April, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
